### `discussion_board_member_profiles`

Member profile information including display name, bio, and profile picture.

Stores publicly visible profile data for each registered member. Each
member has exactly one profile record that is created when the member
account is created. Profile information is independent of authentication
credentials and can be updated by members at any time.

The profile includes the member's public display name (shown as author
attribution on articles and comments), optional biographical information
for community introduction, and a URL reference to the member's profile
picture. All profile modifications are tracked through timestamps for
audit purposes.

When a member account is deleted, the associated profile is also deleted.
This separation of profile data from authentication data allows flexible
profile management while maintaining data integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > Reference to the member account this profile belongs to. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}. Each profile is associated with exactly one
  > member account (1:1 relationship).
- `display_name`
  > Public display name shown as author attribution on articles and comments.
  > Required field, 1-50 characters. Used instead of username for public
  > visibility to protect user privacy.
- `bio`
  > Optional biographical information or 'about me' text. Maximum 500
  > characters. Members can use this to introduce themselves and share
  > relevant expertise or interests related to economic and political
  > discussion.
- `profile_picture_url`
  > URL reference to the member's profile picture. Points to the actual image
  > file stored in the attachment system. Null if no profile picture has been
  > uploaded. Images are automatically resized to 200x200 pixels and EXIF
  > metadata is stripped for privacy.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the profile was created (typically when member account was
  > created). Used for audit trail and member join date tracking. Stored in
  > UTC.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the last profile modification. Updated whenever
  > display_name, bio, or profile_picture_url is changed. Used to track
  > profile update history and for audit purposes. Stored in UTC.

### `discussion_board_member_preferences`

Member account preferences and settings for notifications, display, and
communication.

Stores personal preference settings that control how members receive
notifications, display content, and interact with the platform. Each
member has exactly one preference record that stores their individual
settings for email notifications, notification frequency, display theme,
and other personal preferences.

Notification preferences include options to control email notifications
for article replies, comment replies, moderator actions, and optional
daily digest emails. Display preferences include theme selection (light,
dark, system default). All preferences have sensible defaults to provide
a good out-of-the-box experience while allowing members to customize
based on their needs.

Preference modifications are tracked through timestamps for audit
purposes. These preferences are separate from profile data to maintain
clear separation between public identity (profile) and private settings
(preferences).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > Reference to the member account these preferences belong to. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}. Each preference record is associated with
  > exactly one member account (1:1 relationship).
- `email_notifications_enabled`
  > Master toggle for all email notifications. When false, no email
  > notifications are sent regardless of other preference settings. Default:
  > true to enable notifications. Members can disable to reduce inbox volume.
- `comment_reply_notifications`
  > Whether member receives email notifications when someone replies to their
  > comments. Default: true. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is
  > true.
- `article_reply_notifications`
  > Whether member receives email notifications when someone comments on
  > their articles. Default: true. Only active if email_notifications_enabled
  > is true.
- `article_approval_notifications`
  > Whether member receives email notifications when their submitted articles
  > are approved or rejected by moderators. Default: true. Helps members
  > track publication status of their submissions.
- `moderator_action_notifications`
  > Whether member receives email notifications about moderator actions
  > affecting their content (deletions, edits, etc.). Default: true. Only
  > applies if member's content is actioned by moderators.
- `daily_digest_enabled`
  > Whether member receives optional daily digest emails summarizing new
  > articles and discussions. Default: false (disabled). When enabled, digest
  > is sent daily at a consistent time.
- `display_theme`
  > Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light',
  > 'dark', 'system'. Default: 'system' (follows system preference). Stored
  > as lowercase string for consistent comparison.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when preference record was created (typically when member
  > account was created). All preferences are initialized with defaults at
  > account creation time. Stored in UTC.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the last preference modification. Updated whenever any
  > preference setting is changed by the member. Used for audit trail of
  > preference changes. Stored in UTC.

### `discussion_board_articles`

Discussion articles representing the primary content type on the
platform. Articles are forum discussion threads initiated by members
about economic and political topics. Each article flows through a
moderation workflow before publication, requires moderator approval
before becoming visible to other users, and supports rich content
including text, images, and file attachments.

Articles form the foundation of community discussion. They are the
primary business entities that users create to initiate conversations and
share perspectives. The article lifecycle includes submission, moderator
review, approval/rejection/request for changes, and optional publication.
Published articles accumulate comments from community members, creating
threaded discussions.

Each article maintains a persistent record even after rejection or
archival, supporting audit trails and allowing authors to resubmit
rejected content after revisions. Articles reference their creator
member, assigned category, and moderation status for proper content
discovery and management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the member who created this article. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}
- `discussion_board_category_id`
  > Reference to the category this article belongs to (Economics, Politics,
  > Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other). {@link
  > discussion_board_categories.id}
- `title`
  > Article title or headline. Must be between 5 and 200 characters. Serves
  > as the primary identifier for discussion topic and appears in article
  > lists and search results.
- `body`
  > Article content body containing the main discussion text. Must be between
  > 10 and 50,000 characters. Supports plain text and basic formatting. This
  > is the core content of the discussion article.
- `status`
  > Current publication status of the article. Valid values: pending_approval
  > (submitted but not yet reviewed), published (approved and visible to all
  > users), rejected (did not meet guidelines, visible only to creator and
  > moderators), archived (hidden from public view but retained in system).
  > Determines visibility and editing permissions.
- `view_count`
  > Number of times this article has been viewed by any user. Incremented by
  > 1 each time the article detail page is accessed. Initialized to 0 upon
  > creation. Provides engagement metrics.
- `rejection_reason`
  > Text explanation provided by moderator when article is rejected. Helps
  > article creator understand why content did not meet guidelines and what
  > improvements are needed for resubmission. Maximum 500 characters. Null if
  > article has not been rejected.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when article was initially created. Immutable - never changes
  > even if article is edited. Used for chronological sorting and audit
  > trails.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last modification to article. Updated whenever article
  > content, title, category, or status changes. Used to track edit history
  > and sort by modification recency.
- `published_at`
  > Timestamp when article status changed to published (moderator approval).
  > Null if article is not yet published or was rejected. Records the
  > official publication moment for audit purposes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when article was deleted (soft deletion). Null if article has
  > not been deleted. Enables recovery within retention window and preserves
  > audit trail of deleted content.

### `discussion_board_comments`

Comments represent member responses and engagement on published articles.
Comments enable discussion and debate by allowing members to share
perspectives, ask questions, and respond to article content. Unlike
articles, comments are published immediately without moderation approval,
creating immediate visibility and real-time engagement.

Each comment belongs exclusively to one article and extends that
article's discussion thread. Comments maintain author information,
creation timestamp, and optional attachments (images and files). Comments
support editing for content correction and deletion for content removal,
with soft deletion preserving comment records for audit purposes.

Comments form the interactive component of the discussion platform,
transforming the system from one-way content distribution into
collaborative conversation. They are primary business entities requiring
independent management through search, filtering, and moderation
capabilities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to the parent article this comment belongs to. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the member who created this comment. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}
- `body`
  > Comment text content. Must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Contains
  > the member's response, perspective, or question about the article.
  > Supports plain text with basic formatting.
- `is_deleted`
  > Soft deletion flag indicating whether comment has been deleted. True if
  > deleted by author or moderator; false if active. Allows recovery of
  > deleted comments for audit purposes while hiding them from user views.
  > Defaults to false.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when comment was originally created. Immutable - never changes.
  > Records the exact moment comment was posted for chronological sorting and
  > rate limiting checks.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last edit to comment. Null if comment has never been edited.
  > Updated whenever member modifies comment text or attachments. Allows
  > tracking of comment modifications with edit timestamps displayed to
  > users.

### `discussion_board_attachments`

File and image attachments associated with articles and comments.

Stores metadata for all file and image attachments uploaded to articles
and comments on the discussion board. Each attachment maintains a
reference to its parent content (article or comment) through a
polymorphic relationship pattern.

Attachments support multiple file types including images (JPG, PNG, GIF,
WebP) and documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX, CSV, ODT, ODS, ODP, ZIP).
File validation, malware scanning, and size limiting occur at upload time
to ensure security and prevent abuse.

When parent content (article or comment) is deleted, associated
attachments are automatically removed from storage. Attachments can be
deleted independently by content creators or moderators when removing
specific files from posts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_type`
  > Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Either 'article'
  > (references discussion_board_articles) or 'comment' (references
  > discussion_board_comments). Enables polymorphic relationship without
  > multiple nullable foreign keys.
- `parent_id`
  > UUID of the parent content (article or comment) this attachment is
  > associated with. Combined with parent_type to identify the parent entity.
- `original_filename`
  > Original filename as uploaded by the user (max 255 characters). Used for
  > display in UI and download dialog. May contain spaces and special
  > characters.
- `storage_path`
  > System-generated file path where attachment is stored. Uses secure naming
  > pattern (timestamp_hash_originalname) to prevent directory traversal
  > attacks. Unique across entire system.
- `file_size`
  > File size in bytes. Validated at upload time to ensure limits are
  > enforced (10 MB for images, 25 MB for documents). Used for quota tracking
  > and display to users.
- `mime_type`
  > MIME type of the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf, text/plain).
  > Determined by magic number verification (file header inspection) not file
  > extension, for security.
- `file_hash`
  > SHA-256 hash of file content for integrity verification and malware
  > scanning. Computed at upload time and used to detect file corruption or
  > tampering.
- `is_image`
  > Whether this attachment is an image file. Used to determine display
  > method (embedded inline for images, downloadable link for documents) and
  > whether image dimensions are captured.
- `width`
  > Image width in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image
  > files. Used for display sizing and validation (must be 100-8000 pixels).
- `height`
  > Image height in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image
  > files. Used for display sizing and aspect ratio preservation.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when attachment was uploaded. Immutable after creation. Used
  > for audit trails and display of upload time to users.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last modification. Updated when attachment metadata is
  > modified. Usually equals created_at except when file is replaced or
  > metadata edited.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when attachment was soft-deleted. Null if attachment is active.
  > Soft deletion preserves attachment record for audit purposes while hiding
  > from user views.

### `discussion_board_moderation_actions`

Comprehensive audit trail of all moderation actions taken on discussion
board content. Records every decision to approve, reject, delete, or edit
articles and comments by moderators, with full context including reason
and detailed notes for accountability and audit purposes.

Captures content review workflow where moderators evaluate submitted
articles, approve for publication, request changes, or reject. Also
tracks reactive moderation where moderators delete inappropriate comments
or articles in response to community guidelines violations.

Each action includes the moderator who performed it, the specific content
affected, the type of action taken, and the business reason (rejection
reason, deletion reason, edit notes). This immutable record enables
tracking of moderation patterns, decision consistency, and provides users
with explanation of moderation decisions affecting their content.

Designed as append-only with no updates or deletes - all records
preserved for legal compliance, dispute resolution, and system integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_moderator_id`
  > Reference to the moderator who performed this action. Identifies which
  > moderator approved, rejected, or deleted the content. {@link
  > discussion_board_moderators.id}
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the member who created the content being moderated (article
  > or comment author). Used to track and notify which member's content was
  > moderated. [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members)
- `action_type`
  > Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: 'approved' (article
  > published), 'rejected' (article not approved), 'requested_changes'
  > (feedback for revision), 'deleted_article' (article removed),
  > 'deleted_comment' (comment removed), 'edited_article' (moderator
  > corrected article content), 'edited_comment' (moderator corrected
  > comment), 'flagged' (marked for further review). Determines business
  > outcome and what notifications are sent.
- `content_type`
  > Type of content being moderated. Valid values: 'article' or 'comment'.
  > Indicates whether action applies to an article or comment to enable
  > polymorphic tracking of moderation across content types.
- `content_id`
  > UUID identifier of the content being moderated. References either
  > discussion_board_articles.id or discussion_board_comments.id depending on
  > content_type value. Combined with content_type, enables tracking
  > moderation across both article and comment entities.
- `reason`
  > Business reason for the moderation action in 10-500 characters. For
  > rejections: explains policy violation (e.g., 'Personal attacks on
  > individuals'). For deletions: explains violation category (e.g., 'Spam
  > content'). For requested changes: specific feedback (e.g., 'Add citation
  > for economic data in paragraph 3'). Used to notify affected member and
  > maintain moderation consistency.
- `notes`
  > Optional detailed moderator notes up to 1000 characters for internal
  > record-keeping. May contain context about decision (policy
  > interpretation, precedent, escalation factors). Not necessarily shown to
  > user but available to other moderators and administrators for
  > understanding decision rationale.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when moderation action was performed in UTC. System-generated,
  > immutable. Used to order moderation history chronologically and determine
  > time from content creation to moderation.

### `discussion_board_user_warnings`

Audit trail tracking user account management actions taken by moderators
including warnings, suspensions, and bans. Maintains immutable record of
every disciplinary action, its reason, duration, and auto-reactivation
schedule for account lifecycle management.

Records when moderators warn a member about guideline violations
(creating accountability for repeated issues), suspend accounts
temporarily (blocking posting but allowing viewing), or permanently ban
accounts (preventing all access). Each action is timestamped and
documented with the moderator name and specific reason.

For temporary suspensions, tracks suspension end date and enables
automatic account reactivation when suspension period expires. For
permanent bans, records the ban decision with no auto-reactivation.
Notifications are sent to affected member explaining restriction reason
and duration.

Designed as append-only record for full history of user management
actions, enabling moderators to review account history, understand
escalation patterns, and make consistent decisions about future
violations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the member account being warned, suspended, or banned.
  > Identifies which user is subject to the moderation action. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}
- `discussion_board_moderator_id`
  > Reference to the moderator who issued the warning or initiated the
  > suspension/ban. Tracks accountability for each account management action.
  > [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators)
- `action_type`
  > Type of user account action taken. Valid values: 'warning' (notification
  > about violations), 'suspension' (temporary block from posting, duration
  > specified), 'ban' (permanent block from accessing system). Determines
  > account restrictions and notification message sent to user.
- `reason`
  > Required business reason for the action in 10-500 characters. Examples:
  > 'Repeated policy violations', 'Harassment of other members', 'Spam
  > content creation', 'Offensive language'. Explains to member why action
  > was taken and appears in notification email.
- `notes`
  > Optional detailed moderator notes up to 1000 characters for internal
  > record-keeping. May reference specific violations, previous warnings, or
  > escalation factors informing the decision. Available to other moderators
  > for context on account history.
- `suspension_end_date`
  > For suspension action_type only: timestamp when suspension expires and
  > account should automatically reactivate. NULL for warnings and bans
  > (which have no auto-reactivation). Used by system job to auto-reactivate
  > accounts on expiration.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this warning/suspension is currently in effect. TRUE when first
  > issued. For suspensions: changes to FALSE when suspension expires and
  > auto-reactivation occurs. For bans: remains TRUE indefinitely (never
  > auto-reactivates). For warnings: remains TRUE (warnings don't expire,
  > they accumulate in history).
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when warning/suspension/ban action was issued by moderator in
  > UTC. System-generated, immutable. Used to order account history
  > chronologically and determine suspension start time.

### `discussion_board_reports`

Member reports of inappropriate content for moderator review.

Members can report articles or comments they believe violate community
guidelines. Each report creates a queue item for moderators to
investigate and take action. Reports track the reported content, reason
for the report, reporter identity, and resolution status.

Reports are distinct from moderation actions. A report is user-generated
feedback flagging content; moderation actions are moderator decisions on
what to do about reported content. This separation enables tracking both
member concerns and moderator decisions independently.

Report status progresses through: pending_review (awaiting moderator
investigation) → resolved (moderator took action) or dismissed (moderator
determined no action needed).

All reports are permanent records for audit and moderation history purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: The member who filed this report. [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members)
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to reported article (null if report is for a comment). {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}
- `discussion_board_comment_id`
  > Reference to reported comment (null if report is for an article). {@link
  > discussion_board_comments.id}
- `assigned_moderator_id`
  > Moderator assigned to review this report (null until assignment). {@link
  > discussion_board_moderators.id}
- `reason`
  > Reason for the report. Predefined values: offensive_language,
  > personal_attack, spam, off_topic, copyright_violation, harassment, other.
  > Helps categorize reports for triage and analysis.
- `description`
  > Optional detailed description provided by reporter explaining why they
  > believe content violates guidelines. Maximum 500 characters. Provides
  > context for moderators during review.
- `status`
  > Current status of the report. Values: pending_review (awaiting moderator
  > investigation), resolved (moderator took action), dismissed (moderator
  > reviewed and determined no action needed). Used to track report workflow
  > progression.
- `moderator_notes`
  > Notes added by assigned moderator during review. Maximum 500 characters.
  > Records moderator's investigation findings and reasoning for resolution
  > decision.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when report was submitted by member. Used for audit trail and
  > report age tracking.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when report was last updated (status change, moderator notes
  > added, etc.). Tracks modification history.
- `resolved_at`
  > Timestamp when report was resolved or dismissed by moderator. Null while
  > report is still pending review. Used to calculate resolution time
  > metrics.

text: I'll generate the API interface specification with all the endpoints needed for your discussion board.

operations.specification: Guest user registration endpoint that creates a temporary guest account without credentials. This operation allows unauthenticated visitors to obtain temporary access tokens to view published articles and comments on the discussion board. The guest account is created without requiring email or password authentication, providing immediate read-only access to the platform.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register an unauthenticated guest visitor for temporary read-only access to the discussion board.
operations.description:
The guest registration endpoint creates a temporary guest account that provides immediate read-only access to the discussion board platform. Guest users can view published articles and comments but cannot create content, post comments, upload attachments, or perform any write operations on the platform. This operation is designed to allow unauthenticated visitors to explore the discussion board without requiring account credentials.

Guest accounts are created with a temporary access token and refresh token that allow the user to maintain their session while browsing content. The system generates a unique identifier for each guest session, enabling the platform to track anonymous visitors while respecting their privacy and read-only access restrictions.

Guest users have restricted permissions that prevent them from accessing authenticated-only features. The discussion_board_guests table supports storing basic guest session information including created timestamp for session tracking and temporary token management.

The registration process is public and requires no authentication, making it accessible to any unauthenticated visitor. Guest accounts may have configurable session durations and can be managed through moderation tools if necessary.

Related operations include guest token refresh (GET /auth/guest/refresh) for maintaining active sessions and article retrieval endpoints (GET /articles) that respect guest user read-only permissions.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization response containing temporary access and refresh tokens.

operations.specification: Guest token refresh endpoint that renews temporary access tokens for existing guest sessions. This operation allows guest users to extend their temporary access by exchanging a valid refresh token for a new access token, enabling continuous browsing of published articles and comments without re-registration.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh temporary access tokens for an active guest session.
operations.description:
The guest token refresh endpoint enables guest users to renew their temporary access tokens without requiring re-registration. When a guest's access token expires, they can use their valid refresh token to obtain a new access token, allowing them to continue browsing published articles and comments on the discussion board.

Guest refresh tokens are short-lived credentials that authenticate the guest's existing session. The refresh operation validates the provided refresh token and, if valid, generates a new access token while potentially extending or rotating the refresh token itself. This mechanism allows guests to maintain continuous read-only access while providing security through token expiration.

The guest session information stored in the discussion_board_guests table is updated with new token information when refresh operations occur. The system tracks session lifecycle through timestamps, ensuring that abandoned guest sessions can be identified and cleaned up appropriately.

Guest refresh tokens are subject to configurable expiration windows and may be invalidated if suspicious activity is detected. The refresh operation maintains the same read-only access restrictions as the original guest registration, preventing any privilege escalation or write access.

This operation is a critical component of the guest user authentication flow, working in conjunction with the guest join operation (POST /auth/guest/join) to provide seamless temporary access management. Guest sessions refreshed through this endpoint retain their original created timestamp for session duration tracking.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization response containing renewed access and refresh tokens.

operations.specification: Member user registration endpoint for creating new discussion board accounts. This operation creates a new member record in the discussion_board_members table, generates initial authentication credentials, and issues JWT tokens (access and refresh) for immediate session establishment. The registration process accepts email, username, password, and display name, validates input constraints, checks for duplicate credentials (email and username must be unique), and sends email verification link. Upon successful registration, member account is created with account_status='active' and email_verified=false, requiring email verification before posting privileges are granted.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new member account for the discussion board.
operations.description:
This endpoint creates a new member account in the discussion_board_members table with complete authentication setup. The operation accepts member registration details including email, username, password, and display name. These credentials are validated against business rules: email must be valid format (max 254 characters) and globally unique, username must be 3-30 characters of alphanumeric characters plus hyphens/underscores and globally unique, password must meet complexity requirements, and display name must be 1-50 characters.

The password is immediately hashed using bcrypt with minimum 12 rounds before storage, never storing plain text. The newly created member record is initialized with email_verified=false, account_status='active', and created_at timestamp set to current UTC time. A verification email is generated and sent to the provided email address containing a verification link that member must click to enable article creation and comment posting capabilities.

Upon successful account creation, the operation generates JWT tokens including an access token (short-lived, used for immediate API requests) and a refresh token (long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens). These tokens are issued immediately allowing the newly registered member to interact with the platform, though posting restrictions remain until email verification is completed.

The email field is stored exactly as provided and must not already exist in the discussion_board_members table (unique constraint). The username field is enforced case-insensitive and must not already exist. The display_name field is stored as provided and is displayed publicly as author attribution on articles and comments. The password_hash field stores the bcrypt-hashed result and is never returned to the client.

This operation should be called before any authenticated member operations. Related operations include login for existing members, refresh for token renewal, and email verification endpoints for activating posting privileges after registration.

requestBody.description: Member registration credentials including email, username, password, and display name

responseBody.description: Newly created member account with authentication tokens

operations.specification: Member user login endpoint for authenticating existing discussion board members. This operation validates provided credentials (email or username with password) against the discussion_board_members table, verifies account status permits login, validates password against stored bcrypt hash, and upon successful authentication creates a new session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table with connection context (IP address, URL, referrer). The operation then issues JWT tokens (access and refresh) that grant authentication context to subsequent API requests.
operations.name: login
operations.summary: Authenticate a member and establish a new session.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates an existing member by validating credentials and establishing an authenticated session. The operation accepts either email or username as the login identifier, along with the member's password. The identifier is matched case-insensitively against the discussion_board_members table to locate the member account.

Password validation compares the provided plain text password against the stored password_hash field using bcrypt verification. Passwords must match exactly to authentication to succeed. The account_status field is checked to ensure the member account is in 'active' state; accounts with status 'suspended', 'terminated', or 'deleted' are rejected with appropriate error responses.

Upon successful credential validation, a new session record is created in the discussion_board_member_sessions table capturing connection metadata: the ip field records the IPv4 or IPv6 address of the login request, the href field captures the full URL where login occurred, and the referrer field captures the HTTP Referrer header (may be empty string if unavailable). The session created_at timestamp is set to current UTC time, and expired_at remains null for active sessions. Sessions automatically expire after 7 days.

The email_verified field of the member is checked to determine posting privileges. operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated, and sorted list of discussion board articles. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and supports advanced search capabilities including filtering by status, category, member/creator, and date ranges. The operation implements pagination with configurable page sizes and offset-based navigation, along with sorting by creation date, publication date, title, or view count in ascending or descending order. Full-text search across article titles and body content is supported through GIN indexes.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion board articles from the system. This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for discovering articles based on multiple criteria including publication status (pending_approval, published, rejected, archived), assigned category, article creator/member, date ranges, and full-text search across article titles and body content.

The operation supports sophisticated pagination with configurable page sizes (default 20, max 100) and offset-based navigation for efficient data retrieval. Results can be sorted by creation timestamp, publication timestamp, article title, or view count in ascending or descending order. Multiple sort criteria can be chained for complex ordering requirements.

Articles returned in search results include essential metadata (title, status, creator info, category, timestamps, view count) optimized for list display. The response includes pagination metadata allowing clients to determine total article count, current page position, and navigation to next/previous pages. Article body content is truncated for list views to improve performance.

Security and authorization are enforced based on article status and user authentication. Unauthenticated users see only published articles. Members see published articles plus their own articles in any status. Moderators see all articles regardless of status for review and management purposes. Soft-deleted articles (deleted_at is not null) are excluded from public views but visible to moderators.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering options, pagination parameters, and sorting specifications for article retrieval

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summary information matching search criteria with pagination metadata

operations.specification: This operation creates a new discussion board article in the discussion_board_articles table. A member submits article content (title, body, and optional category) which is initially placed in 'pending_approval' status. The article is assigned to the authenticated member as the creator. Category assignment is required and must reference an existing category from discussion_board_categories table. Upon successful creation, the article record is persisted with timestamps, initialized view_count to 0, and null values for rejection_reason, published_at, and deleted_at. The operation enforces validation rules on title (5-200 characters), body (10-50,000 characters), and category existence.
operations.summary: Create a new discussion board article in pending approval status
operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article to initiate a discussion thread on the platform. This operation allows authenticated members to submit article content for moderator review before publication. The article is created in 'pending_approval' status, meaning it is not visible to other users until a moderator reviews and approves it.

The operation requires three essential inputs: article title (5-200 characters), article body content (10-50,000 characters containing the main discussion text), and category selection from predefined categories (Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other). The authenticated member making the request is automatically assigned as the article creator/author. The article is assigned a unique UUID identifier upon creation.

Initial article state includes creation timestamp (set to current UTC time), updated_at also set to creation time, view_count initialized to 0, and null values for rejection_reason, published_at, and deleted_at. The operation validates that the selected category exists in the discussion_board_categories table before creating the article.

This operation requires authentication - only verified members can create articles. The member's email must be verified (email_verified = true) and account status must be 'active'. Articles submitted by members undergo moderator review workflow where moderators can approve (status → published), reject (status → rejected with optional rejection_reason), request changes, or delete the article. Members can edit their pending articles before moderation approval, and can resubmit rejected articles after revisions.

requestBody.description: Article creation data including title, body content, and category assignment

responseBody.description: Newly created article with all assigned metadata including timestamps, status, and creator information

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: Category must exist before an article can be assigned to it. The article creation requires a valid category_id that references an existing category from the discussion_board_categories table.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a specific discussion board article by its unique identifier from the discussion_board_articles table. The article includes complete details about the discussion topic including title, body content, current status, view count, and moderation information. This operation supports retrieving articles in any status (pending_approval, published, rejected, or archived) based on member permissions and article ownership. The retrieved article contains full context needed for displaying the article detail view including creator information, category assignment, and publication timeline.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific discussion board article by ID
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a single discussion board article from the discussion_board_articles table. This operation fetches the article by its unique identifier and returns comprehensive information including the article title, body content, current publication status, view count, moderation status, rejection reason (if applicable), and timestamps for creation, modification, and publication.

The retrieved article includes metadata about the creator member, assigned category, and moderation workflow state. Articles flow through a moderation process before publication, with possible statuses including pending_approval (awaiting moderator review), published (approved and visible), rejected (did not meet guidelines), and archived (hidden from public view). Rejection reasons are included for rejected articles to help creators understand why their submission was not approved.

This operation enforces appropriate access control based on article status and user role. Published articles are accessible to all users, while pending and rejected articles may be restricted to the article creator and moderators depending on business requirements. Archived articles may require special permissions or may be restricted entirely from regular member access.

View count tracking is maintained separately and reflects the number of times this article detail page has been accessed. Each successful retrieval of this endpoint should increment the view counter to track article engagement metrics. The operation returns all core article fields from the discussion_board_articles table including id, title, body, status, view_count, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at, published_at, deleted_at, discussion_board_member_id, and discussion_board_category_id.

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing discussion board article identified by its unique identifier. The operation modifies article content, title, category assignment, and status fields in the discussion_board_articles table. When articles are updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect the modification time, while created_at and published_at timestamps remain immutable. The operation supports partial updates where only specified fields are modified. Status updates may trigger moderation workflow state changes (e.g., moving from published back to pending_approval for re-review). This operation enforces authorization checks to ensure only the article creator or moderators can modify articles.
operations.summary: Update an existing discussion board article
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board article in the discussion_board_articles table. This operation allows modification of article attributes including title, body content, category assignment, and status. The operation enforces strict authorization - typically only the article creator can edit their own articles, with moderators having additional authority to change status and add rejection reasons.

When an article is updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to record the modification time. However, the created_at and published_at timestamps remain immutable and are never modified, preserving the audit trail of when the article was originally created and officially published by moderators.

operations.description:
Create a new file or image attachment and associate it with a specific discussion board article. This operation handles the complete file upload workflow including validation, storage, and metadata persistence. The operation accepts a file upload with the original filename preserved, validates the file against security and size restrictions, stores it securely with a system-generated path pattern, extracts relevant metadata, and creates a persistent attachment record in the database.

File validation occurs at upload time to ensure security and prevent abuse. Supported file types include images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP with maximum 10 MB size) and documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX, CSV, ODT, ODS, ODP, ZIP with maximum 25 MB size). All files undergo magic number verification (file header inspection) rather than relying on file extensions, ensuring MIME type accuracy. Files exceeding size limits are rejected with descriptive error messages indicating the constraint violation.

For image files, the operation automatically extracts and stores image dimensions (width and height in pixels). Images must have dimensions between 100-8000 pixels in both dimensions. These dimensions are captured and stored in the width and height fields for later use in responsive display sizing and validation purposes.

Attachment metadata stored includes: original filename as uploaded (max 255 characters), system-generated secure storage path using timestamp_hash_originalname pattern to prevent directory traversal attacks, file size in bytes, MIME type determined by magic number verification, SHA-256 hash of file content for integrity verification and malware scanning reference, is_image boolean flag for display method determination, and image dimensions (width/height) for image files only. When the parent article is deleted, associated attachments are automatically removed from storage through cascade operations.

Security considerations include authenticated user requirement, file ownership tracking through the article reference, rate limiting on upload frequency to prevent abuse, and secure file path generation preventing directory traversal or filename collision attacks. The operation is available only to authenticated users who have appropriate permissions to modify the article (typically the article creator or moderators).

The attachment is identified by both the article ID (to scope to a specific article) and the attachment ID (to identify the specific file to delete). This two-level identification ensures users can only delete attachments from articles they have permission to modify.

Permission to delete an attachment is determined by the parent article's permissions: Members can delete attachments from their own unpublished (draft, rejected) articles, but cannot remove attachments from published articles (to prevent retroactive changes to discussion content). Members can also delete attachments from their own comments. Moderators can delete attachments from any article or comment to remove problematic content.

When an attachment is deleted, the associated file is marked as deleted (deleted_at timestamp is set) and is hidden from user views. Moderators retain access to deleted attachments for up to 30 days for audit purposes. After the retention window, the physical file is permanently removed from storage by automated cleanup jobs.

If the parent article is deleted, all associated attachments are automatically soft-deleted along with the article. Attempting to delete an attachment from a published article when not a moderator will result in a permission error.

The operation returns the deleted attachment metadata confirming successful deletion, or an appropriate error if the attachment does not exist, the user lacks permission, or the attachment is already deleted.

Categories are foundational reference data that organize articles by topic (Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other) and support the article discovery workflow through category filtering.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific discussion board category by its identifier
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a discussion board category including its name, slug, description, display order, and active status. This operation provides access to the category metadata stored in the discussion_board_categories table.

Categories are foundational reference data that organize and structure all discussions on the platform. Each category defines a topic area for article classification and supports member navigation and discovery through filtering and browsing capabilities.

The category entity includes metadata for display in the user interface: the display name shown to users, a URL-safe slug identifier for filtering and API reference, a detailed description explaining the category's scope and purpose, a display order for navigation menu organization, and an is_active flag indicating whether the category is currently available for article selection.

This GET endpoint returns a single category identified by its UUID. The category data can be used by UI components to display category information, populate category filters in article lists, or provide context when viewing articles within a specific category.

Categories are read-only from the member perspective (only administrators can modify them through the PUT endpoint). All published articles must belong to exactly one category, so category availability and status directly impact the article creation and filtering workflow.

responseBody.description: Complete category details including name, description, display order, and active status

The PUT endpoint allows modification of category metadata including name, slug, description, display order, and active status. Only administrators can modify category properties. The operation validates the updated category data and returns the modified category entity with updated timestamp.
operations.summary: Update a discussion board category's name, description, and configuration
operations.description:
Update the properties of an existing discussion board category identified by its UUID. This operation modifies category metadata stored in the discussion_board_categories table, including display name, URL slug, description text, display order for navigation sequencing, and the active status controlling category availability.

Categories are foundational reference data that organize articles by topic area. The category system provides the organizational structure for the entire discussion board platform. Categories are maintained by system administrators and cannot be created or deleted by regular members—only modification of existing category properties is permitted through this endpoint.

When updating a category, the operation validates that the new properties meet requirements: name must be unique and 1-50 characters, slug must be unique, URL-safe, and lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, description may be up to 500 characters explaining the category's purpose and scope, display order controls the sequence for category menu display (lower numbers appear first), and is_active controls whether the category is available for article selection.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically recorded when changes are applied. The article_count field (denormalized count of published articles in the category) is maintained automatically by the system and cannot be manually modified through this endpoint.

Categories support the discovery workflow by providing navigation paths complementary to search functionality. When a category's active status is changed to false, the category is hidden from new article selections, but existing articles in the category remain visible and accessible to maintain discussion continuity.

This operation requires administrative privileges. Members cannot modify category properties through the API. The response returns the updated category entity with all modified properties and the updated timestamp reflecting when changes were applied.

responseBody.description: Updated category details reflecting all applied modifications and new timestamp

It operates on the discussion_board_categories Prisma table and removes the category record entirely from the database. The operation is restricted to administrative users only and allows system administrators to remove category entries when they are no longer needed. The deletion is permanent and cannot be reversed, so the API will only allow deletion of categories that have no associated articles or will cascade delete related data according to database constraints.
operations.summary: Delete a discussion board category
operations.description:
Remove a discussion board category from the system. This operation performs a permanent deletion of the specified category record from the discussion_board_categories table. Only administrative users with appropriate permissions can execute this operation to prevent accidental removal of important organizational structures.

The operation requires the category ID as a path parameter to identify which category should be deleted. The system will verify that the category exists before attempting deletion. If the category does not exist or has already been deleted, the operation returns an appropriate error response.

Before deletion, the system checks for database constraints and relationships. If the category has associated articles or other dependencies, the deletion may be prevented depending on the referential integrity rules configured in the database schema. Administrators should ensure categories are not in active use before attempting deletion.

This operation is irreversible—once a category is deleted, it cannot be recovered except through database restoration procedures. Therefore, audit logging and administrative review are recommended before executing this operation in production environments.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target category to delete

operations.specification: This operation updates a discussion board article with new content, metadata, or status information. It operates on the discussion_board_articles Prisma table and allows partial modification of article properties including title, body, category assignment, and status changes. The operation supports modifying article content and facilitating the moderation workflow by updating status from pending_approval to published, rejected, or archived states. The update is restricted to authorized users (creator or moderators) and enforces business rules around status transitions and content validation.
operations.summary: Update a discussion board article
operations.description:
Modify an existing discussion board article's content, metadata, or status. This operation allows updates to article properties including title, body content, category assignment, and publication status. The operation targets the discussion_board_articles table and enforces validation rules to ensure content quality and consistency.

Article updates require proper authorization—creators can modify their own articles (title, body, category), while moderators can additionally change status, add rejection reasons, and manage the moderation workflow. The operation validates that the article exists and that the requesting user has appropriate permissions before proceeding with modifications.

Content validation rules are enforced during updates: titles must be 5-200 characters, body content must be 10-50,000 characters, categories must exist and be active, and status transitions must follow valid workflow paths (pending_approval → published/rejected/archived). If validation fails, the operation returns detailed error information about which fields failed validation and why.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect when the modification occurred. If the status is changed to published, the published_at timestamp is set. The operation returns the updated article with all current properties reflecting the applied changes. Rejection reasons (when applicable) are stored to provide constructive feedback to article creators.

responseBody.description: Updated article with all current properties

operations.specification: This operation implements a global search feature across discussion board content, allowing users to search for articles and comments by keyword. It operates on the discussion_board_articles and discussion_board_comments tables, supporting full-text search with pagination, sorting, and filtering capabilities. The search uses GIN indexes on title, body, and comment body fields for optimized text matching across both published articles and comments.
operations.summary: Search across articles and comments with filtering and pagination
operations.description:
Retrieve search results for articles and comments based on keyword queries across the discussion board platform.

This operation provides comprehensive search functionality allowing members to discover relevant discussions and comments. The search supports full-text matching across article titles, article bodies, and comment content. Results are returned with pagination support to handle large result sets efficiently.

Users can filter results by category, article status (published/pending/rejected), member, date ranges, and other criteria to narrow search results. Results are sorted by relevance by default, with options to sort chronologically (newest/oldest) or by engagement metrics such as view count and comment count.

The search feature is essential for content discovery on the platform, enabling members to find existing discussions before creating new articles and allowing them to follow conversations of interest. Search results include both published articles (visible to all members) and may include comments to surface relevant discussion threads.

Security considerations: Only published articles and non-deleted comments are returned in search results. Articles with rejected or pending status are not searchable by regular members. The operation respects article visibility rules and member permissions—deleted accounts' content is excluded from results. Rate limiting applies to prevent search abuse and excessive database queries.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including keywords, filters, pagination parameters, and sorting options

responseBody.description: Paginated search results containing matching articles and comments with summary information

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of registered members with advanced filtering and search capabilities. It operates on the discussion_board_members table and supports filtering by account status, email verification status, membership duration, and search by username or display name. The operation allows authenticated users to discover community members and provides administrators with member management capabilities.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of discussion board members
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of registered members on the discussion board platform.

This operation provides member discovery and listing functionality supporting both regular members browsing the community and administrators managing member accounts. The operation filters members by account status (active, suspended, terminated) and email verification status to support different use cases. Members can search for other members by username or display name to connect with contributors to specific discussions.

Pagination parameters control result set size and offset for efficient client-side rendering of large member lists. Sorting options allow ordering by membership duration, display name, last login, article count, or other member activity metrics. The operation respects member privacy settings and only returns public member information.

Security considerations: Only verified, active members are visible in public member lists by default. Suspended or terminated accounts are excluded from public discovery but may be visible to administrators. Personal information such as email addresses are never included in list results—only publicly-visible profile information. The operation implements rate limiting to prevent automated member enumeration attacks.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, pagination parameters, and sorting options for member listing

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member information with summary data

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific discussion board member by their unique ID. It accesses the discussion_board_members table to return the member's authentication credentials, account status, profile information, and activity timestamps. The operation provides comprehensive member data including email, username, display name, verification status, account status, creation date, last login, and soft deletion timestamp if applicable.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific discussion board member
operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive profile and account information for a specific discussion board member by their unique identifier. This operation returns complete member details from the discussion_board_members table including authentication-related fields, account status indicators, and temporal tracking information.

The retrieved data includes the member's email address (used for authentication and communication), username (case-insensitive unique identifier), display name (public-facing name for article/comment attribution), email verification status, and current account status (active, suspended, terminated, or deleted). Additionally, the response includes timestamps for account creation, last modification, last login activity, and soft deletion if applicable.

This operation serves as the primary mechanism for retrieving detailed member information after identifying the member through their unique ID. It is typically called after user authentication to retrieve the full authenticated user's profile, or by administrators to view specific member details for moderation or support purposes.

Security context: The actual authorization implementation will determine whether members can view only their own profile or if certain actors (such as moderators or admins) can view any member's profile. The endpoint itself is designed to return complete member information based on the requestor's authorization level.

parameters.name: memberId

responseBody.description: Complete member account information including authentication details, account status, and activity timestamps

It modifies specific fields in the discussion_board_members table such as display name, email address, username, password, and account status. The operation validates all input data according to business rules (email format, username pattern, display name length, etc.) and enforces unique constraints on email and username fields. The updated member record is returned with new timestamps reflecting the modification.
operations.summary: Update profile and account information for a specific discussion board member
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board member's account and profile information. This operation allows modification of key member fields including email address, username, display name, and password. All modifications are validated against business rules to ensure data integrity and enforce unique constraints on email and username fields.

The update operation modifies fields in the discussion_board_members table and automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to reflect when the modification occurred. When password is included in the update, it must be hashed using bcrypt (minimum 12 rounds) before storage. Email and username changes trigger validation to ensure the new values are unique across all members and meet format requirements.

Display name updates are reflected in the member's public profile attribution on articles and comments. Account status can be modified to control member access (values: 'active', 'suspended', 'terminated', 'deleted'). When account_status is set to 'deleted', the deleted_at timestamp is automatically set, implementing soft deletion for audit trail and data retention purposes.

This operation serves as the primary mechanism for members to manage their own accounts and for administrators to perform account modifications (such as suspending or terminating accounts). The updated member record is returned reflecting all changes applied, including the new updated_at timestamp.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target member account to be updated (UUID format)

responseBody.description: Updated member account information with new timestamps reflecting the modification

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a registered member account from the discussion board system. It operates on the discussion_board_members table and performs a complete removal of the member record along with associated profile data. The operation validates that the target member exists, checks authorization to ensure only the member themselves or administrators can delete the account, and then performs the deletion. This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone - member data including email, username, and all associated content references are removed from the system.
operations.summary: Delete a discussion board member account permanently
operations.description:
Delete a registered member account from the discussion board system, removing all member authentication credentials and profile information. This operation removes the member record from the discussion_board_members table, effectively terminating the account and access to the platform.

The deletion process removes the member's email, username, password hash, and all authentication-related data. The operation validates that the requested member exists before attempting deletion and ensures proper authorization - only the member themselves (via authenticated session) or system administrators can delete an account.

This is an irreversible operation that permanently removes member records from the system. The member will no longer be able to authenticate or access the platform after deletion. Any articles or comments created by the member may remain in the system with orphaned author references, depending on application-level cascade policies for content deletion.

Authorization context: The operation requires authentication and validates that the requesting user is either the member being deleted (self-deletion) or has administrative privileges. Attempts to delete other members' accounts without proper authorization will be rejected.

Related operations: Before deleting a member account, you may want to retrieve member details using GET /members/{memberId} to confirm the account. Member profile information stored in discussion_board_member_profiles is managed separately through dedicated profile endpoints.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the profile information for a specific member of the discussion board. It operates on the discussion_board_member_profiles table and returns detailed profile data associated with a member account. The operation queries the profile by member ID and returns the member's public display name, biographical information, and profile picture URL. The profile is a 1:1 relationship with the discussion_board_members table, so each member has exactly one profile record.
operations.summary: Retrieve a member's profile information
operations.description:
Retrieve the public profile information for a discussion board member by their member ID. This operation returns the member's profile data from the discussion_board_member_profiles table, including display name, biographical information, and profile picture URL.

The profile information is publicly visible on the platform and includes the display_name field (1-50 characters) shown as author attribution on articles and comments, an optional bio field (up to 500 characters) where members can introduce themselves and share expertise, and a profile_picture_url that references the member's profile image stored in the attachment system.

Profile pictures are automatically resized to 200x200 pixels and EXIF metadata is stripped during upload for privacy protection. The bio field can contain information relevant to the economic and political discussion topics of the platform.

The profile record is created automatically when a member account is created and maintains a 1:1 relationship with the discussion_board_members table. The created_at timestamp indicates when the profile was created (typically when the member account was registered), and updated_at tracks the most recent modification to any profile field.

This operation is public and does not require authentication, allowing all users (including guests) to view member profile information. The profile data supports community interaction by helping users understand other members' backgrounds and expertise relevant to discussions.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member whose profile information should be retrieved (UUID format)

responseBody.description: The requested member's profile information including display name, bio, and profile picture

The endpoint allows authenticated members to modify their public-facing profile information including display name, biographical content, and profile picture URL. The member being updated is identified by the memberId path parameter, which corresponds to the member_id foreign key in the profile table. The operation validates that the requesting member has authorization to update their own profile and enforces business rules around display name length (1-50 characters) and bio content (maximum 500 characters). The profile picture URL must be a valid URI pointing to an image in the attachment system. This operation updates the updated_at timestamp to reflect when the profile was last modified.
operations.summary: Update a member's profile information including display name, bio, and profile picture
operations.description:
Update an existing member profile with new display name, biographical information, and profile picture URL. This operation allows members to manage their public-facing profile information that is displayed as author attribution on articles and comments throughout the discussion board platform.

The member profile is identified by the memberId path parameter which must correspond to the requesting member's own account ID. Only the profile owner can update their profile information. The operation validates all input data according to business rules: display name must be 1-50 characters, bio is optional and limited to 500 characters maximum, and profile picture URL must be a valid URI if provided. The profile_picture_url field points to image files in the attachment system that have been automatically resized to 200x200 pixels and stripped of EXIF metadata for privacy protection.

When the profile is successfully updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current UTC time, providing an audit trail of when profile modifications occurred. The operation returns the complete updated profile object reflecting all changes made, allowing the client to synchronize with the latest profile state. Related profile data includes the member_id foreign key relationship to the discussion_board_members table, confirming the profile belongs to a valid member account.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves an existing member preferences record from the discussion_board_member_preferences table by member ID. The endpoint returns the complete preference settings for a specific member, including notification preferences (email notifications, reply notifications, article approval notifications, moderator action notifications, daily digest), display theme preference, and audit timestamps. The member is identified by the memberId path parameter which corresponds to the member_id foreign key in the preferences table. Each member has exactly one preference record created when the member account is created, with sensible defaults for all preference fields. The response includes all current preference values that control how the member receives notifications, displays content, and interacts with the platform.
operations.summary: Retrieve member notification and display preferences by member ID
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete preference settings for a specific member from the discussion board platform. This operation fetches all notification and display preferences configured for the member, allowing clients to display current preference state or enable preference management interfaces.

The member preferences are identified by the memberId path parameter which must correspond to a valid discussion_board_members record. Each member has exactly one preference record that is automatically created with sensible defaults when the member account is created. The preferences include comprehensive notification controls with individual toggles for email notifications (master control), comment reply notifications, article reply notifications, article approval notifications, and moderator action notifications. Members can also opt into optional daily digest emails that summarize new articles and discussions.

Display preferences include theme selection with valid options of 'light', 'dark', or 'system' (which follows the user's system preference). These preferences are independent of profile data, maintaining clear separation between public identity information stored in member profiles and private settings stored in member preferences. The operation returns all preference fields including created_at and updated_at timestamps that track when the preference record was created and last modified, providing an audit trail of preference changes.

responseBody.description: Member preference settings including notification and display preferences

operations.specification: This operation updates member notification and display preferences stored in the discussion_board_member_preferences table. The endpoint allows authenticated members to modify their email notification settings (article replies, comment replies, approval notifications, moderator action notifications, daily digest), display theme preference (light/dark/system), and other personal settings. The operation validates the memberId path parameter matches the authenticated user's ID to prevent cross-member preference updates. All preference changes are recorded with an updated_at timestamp for audit purposes. The operation references the discussion_board_member_preferences Prisma model which maintains a 1:1 relationship with the discussion_board_members table.
operations.description:
Update member account preferences and notification settings for a specific member.

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their personal preferences stored in the discussion_board_member_preferences table. Members can control how they receive notifications (email notifications enabled/disabled, notification types for article replies, comment replies, moderator actions, and daily digest preference), and configure their display preferences (theme selection: light, dark, or system default).

The authenticated member can only update their own preferences by providing their memberId in the path. The system validates that the memberId path parameter matches the authenticated user's ID to prevent unauthorized cross-member preference updates. All preference modifications must include only valid preference fields; invalid or unknown fields are rejected.

Preference validation ensures that all boolean notification preference fields (email_notifications_enabled, comment_reply_notifications, article_reply_notifications, article_approval_notifications, moderator_action_notifications, daily_digest_enabled) are either true or false. The display_theme preference must be one of the valid values: 'light', 'dark', or 'system'. Invalid theme values are rejected with descriptive error messages.

When preferences are successfully updated, the system records the change timestamp in the updated_at field to track when preferences were last modified. This timestamp is useful for audit trails and understanding when members made preference changes. The operation returns the complete updated preference object reflecting all current settings after the update is applied.

Related operations that complement preference management: GET /memberPreferences/{memberId} retrieves current preferences for inspection, and PUT /members/{memberId}/password allows members to update their password security separately from preferences.
operations.summary: Update member notification and display preferences for a specific member account

operations.specification: This operation updates the member's password for an authenticated member in the discussion_board_members table. The endpoint requires the member to provide their current password for verification and a new password that meets all password complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters, uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special character). The operation validates that the memberId path parameter matches the authenticated user's ID to prevent cross-member password changes. Password updates trigger immediate session invalidation across all devices to force re-authentication. The new password is hashed using bcrypt with salt rounds of 12 minimum before storage. This operation does not allow password reuse - the system prevents setting a password that matches any of the user's last 3 passwords.
operations.description:
Update the password for an authenticated member's account.

This operation allows members to change their password stored in the discussion_board_members table. The member must provide their current password (for verification that they have legitimate access to the account) and a new password that meets all password complexity requirements. The current password is verified by comparing its bcrypt hash against the stored password_hash field.

Password requirements are strictly enforced: minimum 8 characters in length, must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one numeric digit (0-9), and at least one special character from the set (!@#$%^&*). The system rejects passwords that are fewer than 8 characters, lack required character types, exceed 128 characters, contain the username, contain the email address.

The authenticated member can only update their own password by providing their memberId in the path. The system validates that the memberId path parameter matches the authenticated user's ID to prevent unauthorized password changes on other accounts. When the incorrect current password is provided, the operation denies the change and returns an error without revealing the nature of the mismatch.

Upon successful password change, the system immediately invalidates all existing authentication sessions for that member across all devices and browsers. This forces the member to re-authenticate on all connected devices using their new password, which is a critical security measure. The new password is hashed using bcrypt with a minimum of 12 salt rounds before being stored in the password_hash field. The system prevents password reuse by checking against the member's last 3 passwords - if the new password matches any recent password, the change is rejected.

The operation updates the discussion_board_members.updated_at timestamp to record when the password was changed. Password change operations are logged for security audit purposes. The operation does not return the password or password hash in the response - only confirmation of successful change.

Related operations: PUT /memberPreferences/{memberId} allows updating notification and display preferences separately from password security changes.
operations.summary: Update the password for an authenticated member account with complexity validation and session invalidation
