parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member whose password is being changed. Must match the authenticated user's ID to prevent unauthorized password changes. Format: UUID.

requestBody.description: Current password for verification and new password meeting complexity requirements

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful password change with updated account metadata

operations.specification: This operation updates a member's email address in the discussion_board_members table. The operation requires the authenticated member to provide their current password for verification before allowing the email change. A new email address must be provided, and it must be validated for proper email format and uniqueness across all member accounts. Upon successful email change, the system generates a new email verification code that is sent to the new email address. The member must verify the new email before the change becomes fully active, during which time the old email remains the active login credential. This operation maps directly to the discussion_board_members table and updates the email field while maintaining security by requiring password confirmation.
operations.summary: Update a member's email address with verification requirement
operations.description:
Update the email address associated with a member account in the discussion board system. This is a security-sensitive operation that requires the member to verify their current password before the email can be changed. The new email address must be validated for proper format and uniqueness to prevent duplicate registrations.

When a member initiates an email change, the system validates that the provided email address is in valid RFC 5322 format and that no other member account is already using this email address. The email must not exceed 254 characters. After validation, the system records the new email address in the discussion_board_members table.

Email verification is required for the email change to take full effect. Upon successful email update, the system generates a unique verification token and code valid for 24 hours, then sends a verification email to the new address containing a clickable verification link and alphanumeric verification code. Until the member verifies the new email address, the previous email remains the active login credential.

Once the member verifies the new email through the verification link or code entry, the system marks the email_verified flag as true for the member account. All future authentication and password recovery operations use the newly verified email address.

This operation is restricted to authenticated members and can only be performed on the member's own account. The operation requires the current password as an additional security measure to prevent unauthorized email hijacking. All email changes are logged in the audit trail with the timestamp and member identity for security monitoring and account recovery purposes.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member account whose email will be updated

requestBody.description: Email update request containing new email address and current password for verification

responseBody.description: Updated member account information confirming the email change request and indicating verification requirement

operations.name: updateEmail

prerequisites.description: Member account must be created before email can be updated. The memberId path parameter references an existing member that must have been registered through article creation or authentication flow.

operations.specification: This operation handles uploading a profile picture for a member account stored in the discussion_board_member_profiles and discussion_board_attachments tables. The operation accepts an image file upload from an authenticated member and stores it in the attachment system. The image file must be in JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP format and not exceed 5 MB in size. The system automatically resizes the image to 200x200 pixels for consistent profile display across the platform. Upon successful upload, the system updates the discussion_board_member_profiles table with the profile_picture_url field pointing to the newly stored image, and creates a corresponding attachment record in discussion_board_attachments with parent_type='profile' and the member's profile as the parent. The operation returns the updated member profile with the new profile picture URL.
operations.summary: Upload and set a profile picture for a member account
operations.description:
Upload a profile picture for a member's discussion board account. This operation allows authenticated members to upload a new profile picture that will be displayed with their articles, comments, and public profile page throughout the platform.

The profile picture must be an image file in one of the supported formats: JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP. The file size must not exceed 5 MB. The system validates the file type by inspecting the file header (magic number) rather than relying on file extension for security purposes. Upon upload, the system automatically processes the image: resizing it to a standard 200x200 pixel dimension for consistent display, stripping any EXIF metadata to protect privacy, and computing a SHA-256 hash of the file content for integrity verification.

The uploaded image is stored in the secure attachment storage system with a system-generated filename following the pattern timestamp_hash_originalname to prevent directory traversal attacks and ensure unique storage paths. The original filename provided by the member is preserved for audit purposes.

Upon successful upload, the system updates the member's profile record in the discussion_board_member_profiles table, setting the profile_picture_url field to point to the newly stored image. A corresponding attachment record is created in the discussion_board_attachments table with parent_type='profile' to track all profile picture uploads for audit purposes. The operation is restricted to authenticated members and can only be performed on the member's own profile picture.

If the member already has a profile picture, the new upload replaces the previous image. The previous image file may be automatically cleaned up from storage after a grace period. If the member wants to remove their profile picture entirely, they would need to use a separate delete operation rather than uploading a blank or placeholder image.

The operation returns the updated member profile information including the new profile_picture_url, allowing the client to immediately display the uploaded picture to confirm successful upload.

operations.specification: This operation removes the profile picture associated with a member account in the discussion_board_member_profiles table. When a member deletes their profile picture, the profile_picture_url field is set to null, reverting the profile to display a default avatar placeholder. This is a destructive operation that requires authentication and ownership verification—members can only delete their own profile pictures. The operation updates the member's profile updated_at timestamp to track the modification.
operations.summary: Delete a member's profile picture from their discussion board profile
operations.description:
Remove the profile picture associated with a specific member account. This operation sets the profile_picture_url field to null in the discussion_board_member_profiles table, causing the member's avatar to revert to a system default placeholder.

Authentication and authorization are enforced to ensure members can only delete their own profile pictures. Attempting to delete another member's profile picture returns a 403 Forbidden error with message "You do not have permission to modify this profile."

The profile_picture_url field in discussion_board_member_profiles stores a URI reference to the member's profile picture. When deleted, this field becomes null, and the system displays the default avatar in all locations where the member's profile picture appears (article author attribution, comment author display, profile view, etc.).

Upon successful deletion, the profile's updated_at timestamp is updated to the current UTC time, creating an audit trail of the modification. The operation does not delete the actual image file from storage—that cleanup happens asynchronously after confirmation that no other references exist.

If the member has no profile picture currently set (profile_picture_url is already null), the operation succeeds with HTTP 200 OK, treating it as an idempotent operation. No error is returned for deleting a non-existent profile picture.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member whose profile picture is being deleted. Must match the authenticated user's member ID from the JWT token.

operations.specification: This operation terminates the authenticated member's current session by invalidating the JWT refresh token and clearing authentication credentials. The operation targets the discussion_board_member_sessions table, marking the session's expired_at field with the current timestamp. This implements secure logout functionality that invalidates the user's authentication across all API requests. The operation must receive a valid access token in the Authorization header and uses the authenticated user's ID extracted from the token claims.
operations.summary: Logout an authenticated member and terminate their current session
operations.description:
Terminate the authenticated member's current session and invalidate their authentication credentials. This operation marks the session record in discussion_board_member_sessions as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current UTC time.

Authentication is required for this operation. The member must provide a valid JWT access token in the Authorization header (Bearer scheme). The authenticated user's member ID is extracted from the token claims (JWT sub claim or user context) and used to identify which session to terminate.

When logout is processed, the system performs the following actions: (1) Locate the member's active session (where expired_at is null), (2) Set the expired_at field to current timestamp, (3) Blacklist the member's refresh token to prevent reuse, (4) Clear any session cookies on the client side (via Set-Cookie header with Max-Age=0), (5) Record the logout event in audit logs with timestamp.

After logout succeeds, the member must authenticate again by providing email/username and password to obtain new tokens. All subsequent API requests using the invalidated access token will return HTTP 401 Unauthorized with message "Token expired or invalid. Please log in again."

The operation supports concurrent sessions—logging out from one device/browser only invalidates that specific session. Other active sessions on different devices remain valid and unaffected. For example, if a member is logged in on desktop and mobile, logout on desktop invalidates only the desktop session; the mobile session remains active.

If the member has no active session (all sessions already have expired_at timestamps), the operation still succeeds with HTTP 200 OK, treating logout as idempotent. No error is returned for logging out when already logged out.

WHEN a member's password is changed, THE system SHALL invalidate all refresh tokens associated with that member account, forcing re-login on all devices.
operations.name: logout

prerequisites.description: Member must be authenticated with an active session before they can logout. A valid access token is required to identify which session to terminate.

operations.specification: This operation verifies a member's email address using a verification token or code sent during registration. The operation validates the provided token/code against stored verification data, checks expiration, and marks the member's email as verified in the discussion_board_members table. Upon successful verification, the member gains full posting privileges (ability to create articles and post comments). This operation is associated with the discussion_board_members table and supports the email verification workflow required before members can participate in discussions.
operations.summary: Verify a member's email address using verification token or code
operations.description:
This operation completes the email verification process for newly registered members. When a member registers, the system sends a verification email containing a unique token or alphanumeric code. This endpoint allows the member to submit that token or code to prove ownership of their email address.

The verification process is critical to the discussion board's security and participation model. Members with unverified emails cannot create articles or post comments, ensuring only legitimate email addresses are used for account creation. The system must validate that the provided token or code matches stored verification data and has not expired (24-hour validity window).

Upon successful verification, the system updates the discussion_board_members table, setting email_verified to true. This immediately enables the member to create articles and post comments. The verification token is cleared from storage after successful use to prevent replay attacks.

If verification fails (invalid code, expired code, or already verified), the system returns a specific error message indicating the issue. Expired tokens trigger an offer to resend verification email, making the recovery path clear to users.

This operation requires member authentication context to identify which member is verifying their email. The authenticated member submitting the request must match the member_id associated with the verification data. This prevents one member from verifying another member's email address.

Related operations: POST /auth/member/resend-verification (to request new verification email if code expires), which shares the same workflow context and may be called before or after this verification attempt.
operations.name: verifyEmail

requestBody.description: Email verification token or code provided by the member

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful email verification with member details

prerequisites.description: A member account must be created before email verification can be completed. The verify-email operation requires an authenticated member context to identify which member is verifying their email address.

operations.specification: This operation generates and sends a new verification email to a member's registered email address. The operation creates a fresh verification token (valid for 24 hours) and alphanumeric code, invalidating any previous verification code. The new verification email is sent containing both the token (for link-based verification) and code (for manual entry). This operation is associated with the discussion_board_members table and supports the email verification workflow when original verification emails are lost or the token expires.
operations.summary: Request a new email verification code and email
operations.description:
This operation handles the resend verification email workflow for members who lost the original verification email, entered an incorrect code too many times, or the original verification code expired (24-hour validity window). Members can request a new verification email containing a fresh token and code.

The operation enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse—members can request resend at most once per 5 minutes per account. If a member attempts to resend more frequently, the system returns an error message indicating they must wait before requesting another verification email.

When a resend is requested, the system generates a new verification token and code, invalidating the previous token/code pair. This prevents confusion from multiple valid tokens in circulation. The new verification email is sent immediately to the member's registered email address with clear instructions for completing verification.

The resend operation updates the verification data in the discussion_board_members table (or verification tracking table if implemented separately). The email_verified flag remains false until successful verification using the new code. The member continues to have read-only access but cannot create articles or post comments until email verification is completed.

This operation requires member authentication to identify which member is requesting the resend. The authenticated member submitting the request must have an account in discussion_board_members with unverified status (email_verified = false). Members with already-verified emails can still call this endpoint, which returns a success message for security reasons (preventing account enumeration attacks).

Rate limiting context: Failed attempts to resend (due to rate limiting) should be tracked separately from successful resends. The 5-minute window resets from the timestamp of the most recent resend request by that member.

Related operations: POST /auth/member/verify-email (the endpoint that consumes the verification code sent by this operation), which should be called after the member receives and enters their verification code.
operations.name: resendVerification

responseBody.description: Confirmation that verification email has been sent (generic message for security)

prerequisites.description: A member account must be created before verification emails can be resent. The resend-verification operation requires an authenticated member account to send the verification email to the registered email address.

operations.specification: This operation initiates the password reset workflow for a member who has forgotten their password. The endpoint accepts an email address, validates that a member account exists with that email, generates a secure password reset token valid for 1 hour, and sends a password reset email containing a secure reset link. This operation is associated with the discussion_board_members table and implements the password recovery flow specified in the user account management requirements.
operations.summary: Request password reset via email for a discussion board member account
operations.description:
Initiates the password reset workflow for members who have forgotten their password. When a member provides their email address, the system validates that an account exists with that email, generates a cryptographically secure password reset token with 1-hour expiration, and sends a password reset email containing a secure reset link and instructions.

Security considerations: The system deliberately does not reveal whether an account exists with the provided email address. This prevents account enumeration attacks where bad actors could discover which email addresses are registered. The confirmation message displayed to the user is identical regardless of whether the email exists in the system.

The password reset token is valid for exactly 1 hour from generation. After 1 hour, the token expires and the user must request a new password reset. The reset token is stored securely and validated when the user clicks the reset link in their email.

This operation relates to the discussion_board_members table, specifically the email field which must match exactly (case-insensitive) and the password_hash field which will be updated when the member confirms the reset. The system records the password reset request timestamp for security audit purposes.

The password reset workflow is the first step in a two-step process. After the member receives the email and clicks the reset link, they proceed to the password-reset-confirm endpoint to set their new password. The reset token ensures that only the member who owns the email address can complete the password reset.

Rate limiting is enforced to prevent abuse: members can request password reset emails a maximum of once per 5 minutes per email address.

requestBody.description: Member email address for password reset request

responseBody.description: Confirmation response for password reset request (generic message regardless of email existence for security)

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: This operation completes the password reset workflow for a member who has received a password reset email. The endpoint accepts a valid password reset token, the new password, and password confirmation. The system validates the reset token (not expired, not already used), verifies the new password meets all complexity requirements, hashes the new password, updates the member's password_hash in the discussion_board_members table, invalidates all existing sessions for that member, and sends a confirmation email. This operation is the second step in the password recovery flow specified in user account management requirements.
operations.summary: Confirm password reset and set new password for a discussion board member
operations.description:
Completes the password reset workflow by validating the reset token received in the password reset email and allowing the member to set a new password. When a member clicks the reset link in their email, they are directed to a form containing the reset token. The member enters a new password and confirmation, then submits this operation.

Token validation: The system validates that the reset token is valid (matches stored token), has not expired (1-hour window from request), and has not been previously used. If the token is invalid or expired, the operation returns an error directing the member to request a new password reset.

Password requirements enforcement: The new password must meet all complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one numeric digit, at least one special character from {!@#$%^&*}. The password cannot contain the member's email address or username. The password cannot match any of the member's last 3 passwords (password reuse prevention). If the new password fails any requirement, the operation returns a specific error message indicating which requirements are not met.

Password confirmation: The new password must exactly match the password confirmation field. If they do not match, the operation returns an error and requires the user to re-enter both password fields.

Database updates: Upon successful validation, the system hashes the new password using bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds and updates the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table. The updated_at timestamp is updated to the current time. The reset token is invalidated (removed from storage) to prevent reuse.

Session invalidation: All existing authentication sessions for the member are immediately terminated. This forces the member to log in again on all devices using their new password. All existing JWT refresh tokens are blacklisted.

Notification: A confirmation email is sent to the member's registered email address confirming that their password has been reset.

Relationship to discussion_board_members table: This operation updates the password_hash and updated_at fields for the member identified by the reset token. The operation indirectly affects discussion_board_member_sessions table by invalidating sessions.

This is the second operation in a two-step password reset process. The password-reset-request operation must be executed first to generate and email the reset token.

requestBody.description: Password reset token and new password details for confirmation

responseBody.description: Confirmation response for successful password reset

operations.name: confirmPasswordReset

prerequisites.description: A password reset token must be generated and sent to the member's email address via the password-reset-request operation before the confirmation step can be completed. The token received in the email is required to validate the member's identity and authorize the password change.

operations.specification: This operation allows authenticated members to securely change their account password. The member must provide their current password for verification before a new password can be set. The new password must meet all security complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters, uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special characters). Upon successful password change, all existing sessions for the member are invalidated, forcing re-authentication on all devices for security purposes. This operation directly modifies the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table, following the bcrypt hashing algorithm with minimum 12 salt rounds. The operation is associated with the discussion_board_members Prisma table and follows the secure password management workflow defined in the user account management requirements.
operations.summary: Change authenticated member's account password with current password verification
operations.description:
Allows an authenticated member to change their account password securely. The member must provide their current password for verification to prevent unauthorized password changes. The new password must meet all complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one numeric digit, and at least one special character from the set: !@#$%^&*. The new password must not be a commonly used password or contain the member's username or email address.

When the password change request is submitted with valid credentials, the system updates the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table using bcrypt hashing with a minimum of 12 salt rounds. The operation enforces that the new password has not been used in the member's previous 3 password changes, preventing password reuse vulnerabilities.

Upon successful password change, the system automatically invalidates all existing sessions for the member by removing all corresponding entries from the discussion_board_member_sessions table. This forces the member to re-authenticate on all devices, ensuring that only the member with the new password can access their account. This security measure protects against compromised sessions from stolen or exposed devices.

Security considerations include: the operation requires HTTPS/TLS encryption for all communication, the current password is verified using bcrypt hash comparison (never plain text comparison), and the operation is protected against brute-force attacks through rate limiting. Failed password change attempts are logged for security auditing.

If the current password is incorrect, the operation returns an error without revealing that the password was wrong (to prevent account enumeration). If the new password fails complexity requirements, specific error messages indicate which requirements are not met. Successful password changes are logged in the audit trail with timestamp and member ID.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated member whose password is being changed (from JWT token)

requestBody.description: Password change request containing current password for verification and new password meeting all complexity requirements

responseBody.description: Confirmation message indicating password has been successfully changed and all sessions have been invalidated

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: This operation retrieves all active authentication sessions for the authenticated member. Sessions represent login instances from different IP addresses or devices. The operation returns comprehensive session details including IP address, creation timestamp, and last activity timestamp. This allows members to monitor their active sessions across all devices (desktop, laptop, mobile, etc.) and identify potentially suspicious or unknown login locations. The operation queries the discussion_board_member_sessions table, filtering for sessions belonging to the authenticated member with null expired_at values (indicating active sessions). Members can use this information to detect unauthorized access or logout from unwanted sessions. This operation is associated with the discussion_board_member_sessions Prisma table.
operations.summary: Retrieve all active authentication sessions for the authenticated member
operations.description:
Returns a list of all active authentication sessions for the authenticated member, allowing members to monitor and manage their login activity across devices. Each session represents a distinct login instance from a specific IP address or device.

The operation queries the discussion_board_member_sessions table and returns detailed information about each active session including: IP address of login origin (for geographic and device identification), full URL where login occurred (for context about access), HTTP referrer (source of authentication request), creation timestamp (when login occurred), and optional last activity timestamp. Sessions are ordered reverse-chronologically with most recent sessions first.

Members can use this endpoint to identify all devices currently authenticated with their account, detect unexpected login locations or IP addresses, and find sessions to logout from (delete) if they identify suspicious activity. This is particularly useful for security monitoring, as members can spot potential account compromise by unusual login locations or device types.

Active sessions are identified by null expired_at timestamp in the discussion_board_member_sessions table. Sessions automatically expire after 7 days of inactivity or when the member explicitly logs out. Members can manually terminate individual sessions through a separate logout endpoint if desired.

The response includes metadata about each session such as IP address (useful for identifying device or location), URL context (where on the site login occurred), and timestamp (for timeline of access). If a member has never logged in or all sessions have expired, the operation returns an empty list with appropriate metadata.

Security note: Members should regularly review their active sessions and logout from sessions they do not recognize. The system does not require additional authentication to view this information since it helps members maintain account security by detecting unauthorized access.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated member whose sessions are being retrieved (from JWT token)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of active authentication sessions for the member with connection details and timestamps

operations.specification: This operation deletes a specific member authentication session from the system, invalidating the JWT refresh token and terminating the user's login context. It operates on the discussion_board_member_sessions table which stores authentication session records with context information (IP address, referrer, URL). When a session is deleted, the expired_at timestamp is set to the current moment, marking the session as inactive. This operation supports the logout workflow where members explicitly end their authenticated session, or moderator/system actions that revoke specific sessions due to security concerns.
operations.summary: Delete a specific member authentication session and invalidate the associated tokens
operations.description:
This operation terminates an active member authentication session and invalidates the associated JWT refresh token. When a member logs out or a session is revoked, this endpoint marks the session as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current time.

The session parameter identifies the specific login instance to terminate. Each member can maintain multiple concurrent sessions across different devices; deleting one session affects only that specific device/login context while preserving other active sessions. The operation is idempotent - attempting to delete an already-expired session returns success without error.

Security considerations include verifying that the authenticated member requesting deletion owns the session being terminated. Members can only delete their own sessions; moderators with appropriate permissions may delete any member's sessions for administrative purposes. The operation logs the deletion event including session ID, member ID, moderator ID (if applicable), and timestamp for audit purposes.

Upon successful deletion, the member must obtain new authentication tokens via the login endpoint to resume access. Any outstanding access tokens remain valid until their natural expiration (15 minutes); only the refresh token becomes invalid. Clients should immediately discard both tokens upon receiving success response from this endpoint.

This operation integrates with the JWT token invalidation and blacklisting system. The session's refresh token is added to the token blacklist, preventing token refresh attempts from generating new access tokens. The session record is retained (soft deletion via expired_at timestamp) to preserve the audit trail and security history.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member session to delete (UUID format)

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation validates whether a provided JWT access token is currently valid and has not been tampered with, expired, or blacklisted. It operates on the discussion_board_member_sessions table indirectly by checking token validity and session status. The operation performs cryptographic signature verification using HMAC-SHA256 with the server's signing secret, verifies token expiration timestamps against the current time, and checks that the session associated with the token (if tracking sessions for this validation) has not been revoked. This supports client-side token validation, SDK token refresh decision-making, and debugging of authentication issues.
operations.summary: Validate a member's JWT access token for authenticity and current validity
operations.description:
This operation validates whether a provided JWT access token is authentic, unmodified, and currently valid. It is used by clients to verify token state before attempting API requests, enabling optimized token refresh decisions and improved user experience through early detection of invalid or expired tokens.

The operation accepts a JWT access token in the request body and performs comprehensive validation checks. First, it verifies the token signature using the server's HMAC signing secret, ensuring the token has not been tampered with or forged. Second, it validates that the token has not expired by comparing the exp claim against the current timestamp. Third, it verifies the token structure contains required claims (userId, email, username, role, etc.) with proper values.

Security considerations include protecting the signing secret and never exposing it to client code. The operation does not require authentication (members can validate tokens before logging in), but it operates on the same token validation logic used internally by protected endpoints. Invalid tokens receive a detailed response explaining the specific validation failure for debugging purposes.

The response indicates token validity status with specific failure reasons if validation fails. Valid tokens return success confirmation with decoded claims. Expired tokens return a specific error code enabling clients to trigger token refresh via the refresh endpoint. Tampered or malformed tokens return security warnings. The operation is stateless and does not depend on session database lookups for basic cryptographic validation.

This operation integrates with the JWT token system defined in user authentication requirements. It supports the client-side token validation workflow where SDKs check token validity before making requests, improving performance by avoiding unnecessary failed API calls and enabling proactive token refresh.

requestBody.description: JWT access token to validate

responseBody.description: Token validation result with validity status and decoded claims if token is valid

operations.specification: This operation logs out an authenticated moderator by invalidating their current session. It operates on the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table, removing the active session record for the requesting moderator. The operation accepts a POST request from an authenticated moderator and terminates their administrative access session, requiring re-authentication to perform further moderation tasks.
operations.summary: Terminate the current moderator authentication session and invalidate login credentials
operations.description:
Logs out the authenticated moderator by invalidating their current session. This operation removes the active moderator session, forcing re-authentication on the next moderation request. The session termination is recorded with the logout timestamp in the expired_at field of the discussion_board_moderator_sessions record.

Security Context: This operation requires an authenticated moderator with an active session. The system identifies the moderator from the JWT token in the Authorization header and invalidates only that specific session, allowing the moderator to maintain other concurrent sessions on different devices if desired.

Session Management: The operation performs a soft termination of the session by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current UTC time. The session record is retained in the database for audit purposes, maintaining a complete history of moderator access. When the logout succeeds, authentication tokens become invalid and subsequent API requests from that session will be rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

Audit Trail: The session termination event is recorded in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table with the precise expiration timestamp. This creates an immutable audit record of when the moderator ended their session, supporting security monitoring and accountability requirements.

Related Operations: The logout operation should be used when a moderator intentionally ends their administrative session. To retrieve information about current and past sessions, use the GET /auth/moderator/sessions operation to view session history and login details.
operations.name: logout

operations.specification: This operation retrieves all authentication sessions (both active and expired) for the currently authenticated moderator. It queries the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to return a paginated list of sessions with connection details including IP address, login URL, referrer, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. The operation provides complete session history for security auditing and managing concurrent sessions.
operations.summary: Retrieve all authentication sessions for the authenticated moderator including active and historical sessions
operations.description:
Retrieves a comprehensive list of all authentication sessions for the currently authenticated moderator. This includes both active sessions (with null expired_at) and historical sessions that have been terminated through logout or automatic expiration. The operation returns paginated results with optional filtering and sorting capabilities.

Session Information Returned: Each session record includes the IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) from which the moderator logged in, the full URL/URI where the login occurred, the HTTP Referrer header value, the session creation timestamp (created_at), and the session termination timestamp if applicable (expired_at). This comprehensive connection context enables moderators to identify and manage their own sessions.

Security & Audit: Sessions from the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table are indexed by moderator ID and creation timestamp, enabling efficient retrieval of a moderator's complete session history. The immutable created_at field records exactly when each session began, while the nullable expired_at field indicates whether a session is currently active (null) or has been terminated.

Concurrent Sessions: Moderators can maintain multiple concurrent sessions across different devices and locations. This operation displays all sessions simultaneously, allowing the moderator to see where they are logged in and when each session was established. This is useful for security monitoring to detect unauthorized access or unexpected login locations.

Pagination & Filtering: The operation supports pagination parameters (page, pageSize) and optional filtering/sorting by creation date, expiration date, or IP address. Results are typically sorted in reverse chronological order (newest sessions first) to show recent activity prominently.

When a moderator deletes a session (typically their own session for logout), the system records the termination timestamp in the expired_at field, making the session inactive. This operation implements session cleanup and logout functionality for moderator authentication sessions.
operations.summary: Terminate a moderator authentication session by ID
operations.description:
This operation allows a moderator to terminate their active session, effectively logging them out from the moderation dashboard. The session ID corresponds to a record in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table that tracks the moderator's login context including IP address, access URL, and referrer information.

When the session is deleted, the system updates the expired_at timestamp field to mark the session as terminated. This prevents further API requests using tokens associated with this session. The moderator's refresh token for this session is also invalidated immediately, requiring re-authentication to access moderation features again.

Security Context: Only the moderator who owns the session can terminate their own session. Moderators cannot terminate other moderators' sessions. This operation requires a valid access token proving the requester's identity and matching the session's moderator association.

Session Cleanup: The operation does not permanently delete the session record from the database. Instead, it marks the session with an expiration timestamp (expired_at), preserving the session history for audit and security logging purposes. This audit trail allows administrators to review moderator login and logout patterns for compliance and security monitoring.

Related Operations: This operation works in conjunction with POST /auth/moderator/validate-token to check session validity. Members typically call this endpoint explicitly during logout, or the system may invalidate expired sessions automatically based on the 7-day session expiration policy.

operations.specification: This operation validates whether a moderator's current authentication token and associated session are still active and valid. It checks the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to verify that the session has not been terminated (expired_at is null) and has not exceeded the 7-day expiration window. This operation is used to maintain session state and determine if re-authentication is needed.
operations.summary: Validate a moderator's authentication token and active session
operations.description:
This operation validates that a moderator's authentication token is still valid and their associated session remains active. The operation requires the moderator to include their current access token in the Authorization header (Bearer token format).

Validation Process: The system performs the following checks on the provided token: (1) Verifies the token signature using the configured signing secret, (2) Checks that the token has not expired by comparing the exp claim against current time, (3) Extracts the moderator ID from the token claims, (4) Queries the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to confirm an active session exists for that moderator, (5) Verifies the session's expired_at field is null (indicating an active, non-terminated session), (6) Confirms the moderator's account_status in discussion_board_moderators table is 'active'.

Token Structure: The access token contains JWT claims including userId (moderator ID), email, username, displayName, role ('moderator'), emailVerified status, issued-at timestamp (iat), and expiration timestamp (exp). The token is signed using HS256 algorithm with a secure secret key.

Session Management: Sessions represent individual logins and can persist across multiple API requests. A moderator can have multiple concurrent sessions (e.g., logged in from different devices). Each session has a unique ID and tracks the IP address, URL, and referrer from which the session originated. Sessions are marked expired after 7 days of creation or when explicitly terminated via DELETE /auth/moderator/sessions/{sessionId}.

Error Handling: If the token is invalid, expired, or the corresponding session is inactive, the operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized. If the moderator account has been suspended or terminated (account_status != 'active'), the operation denies validation even if the token appears valid. This ensures immediate revocation of access when a moderator role is removed.

Use Cases: This operation is typically called by the client periodically or when accessing protected resources to determine if session refresh is needed. If validation fails, the client knows to request a new token using the refresh token endpoint or prompt the moderator to log in again.

requestBody.description: Token validation request with the moderator's current access token

responseBody.description: Validation result indicating whether the token and session are active, with moderator details if valid

operations.specification: This operation creates a warning record for a member account due to policy violation or community guideline breach. The operation associates a moderator-issued warning with a specific member, records the reason for disciplinary action, and optionally stores detailed moderator notes. The warning is logged in the discussion_board_user_warnings table and triggers a notification email to the warned member explaining the violation and next steps. Multiple warnings accumulate in a member's history, informing moderators about escalation patterns and helping establish consistent enforcement of community standards. This operation does not restrict member access—warnings serve as documentation and communication tool before account suspension or termination.
operations.description:
Issue a formal warning to a member account due to policy violations or community guideline breaches. This operation documents moderator-initiated disciplinary action without immediately restricting member access, serving as a first escalation step before potential account suspension.

The warning action is recorded in the discussion_board_user_warnings table with action_type of 'warning', capturing the moderator identity, warning reason, and optional detailed notes. The operation maintains an immutable audit trail of all disciplinary actions for accountability and consistency review. Warnings accumulate in a member's moderation history, allowing moderators to review escalation patterns and understand the context for more severe actions like suspension or termination.

When a warning is issued, the system SHALL send a notification email to the warned member's registered email address explaining the policy violation, the specific reason for the warning, and what behavior changes are expected. The email includes information about potential consequences of continued violations (suspension, then termination). Members can view their warning history in their account settings to understand their moderation status.

When a moderator issues a warning, they must provide a business reason (10-500 characters) explaining the violation category or specific problematic behavior. Optional moderator notes (up to 1000 characters) allow detailed context-setting for other moderators reviewing this member's history, such as references to previous violations, specific comments/articles that triggered the warning, or escalation justification.

Warnings persist indefinitely in the member's moderation history and do not auto-expire. They serve as permanent record of disciplinary actions, enabling moderators to track patterns across extended timeframes. The warning does not automatically restrict member posting rights—members continue to participate normally. However, repeated warnings form the basis for escalation to suspension or termination actions.

This operation is exclusively available to moderator accounts. Only users with moderator role can issue warnings through this endpoint. Member accounts attempting to access this endpoint receive HTTP 403 Forbidden response.
operations.summary: Issue a warning to a discussion board member for policy violations or guideline breaches

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member account being warned

requestBody.description: Warning details including reason and optional moderator notes

responseBody.description: Confirmation of warning issuance with full warning record details

operations.specification: This operation suspends a member account temporarily, restricting their ability to post new articles or comments while allowing them to view existing content. Suspension serves as an escalation from warnings when members continue violating guidelines. The operation records suspension details in the discussion_board_user_warnings table with action_type of 'suspension', including the suspension end date for automatic account reactivation. The member account status is updated to 'suspended' in the discussion_board_members table, preventing login and content creation. A suspension notification email is sent to the suspended member explaining the reason, duration, and instructions for appeal if applicable.
operations.description:
Temporarily suspend a member account due to repeated or severe policy violations, preventing article creation and comment posting while preserving viewing access. This operation escalates account restrictions beyond warnings when members continue violating community guidelines despite previous warnings or commit serious single violations.

The suspension action is recorded in the discussion_board_user_warnings table with action_type of 'suspension', capturing the moderator identity, suspension reason, suspension end date (for automatic reactivation), and optional moderator notes. The operation also updates the member's account_status field in discussion_board_members to 'suspended', which triggers business logic to prevent login and restrict posting privileges system-wide.

When a member account is suspended, the system SHALL:
- Prevent the suspended member from logging into their account
- Prevent the suspended member from creating new articles
- Prevent the suspended member from posting new comments
- Allow the suspended member to view published articles and comments (read-only access)
- Allow the suspended member to view their own unpublished/rejected articles
- Send a notification email to the suspended member's registered email address explaining the suspension reason, exact suspension end date/time (in UTC), and instructions for what to do

The moderator must provide a business reason for suspension (10-500 characters) selecting from predefined categories or custom text. Predefined categories include: 'Repeated Violations', 'Harassment', 'Spam', 'Hate Speech', 'Copyright Violation', or 'Other'. Optional moderator notes (up to 1000 characters) provide internal documentation of the suspension rationale for other moderators' reference.

The moderator must specify the suspension duration through the suspension_end_date parameter. Suspension periods typically range from 7 days to 30 days for temporary suspensions. The suspension_end_date must be a future timestamp in UTC format. The system automatically reactivates the account at the specified date/time, updating account_status back to 'active' and sending a notification to the member that their suspension has expired.

Temporary suspensions are designed as graduated enforcement tool—they restrict posting privileges while preserving account data and allowing eventual return to participation. The automatic reactivation mechanism removes administrative burden of manual account restoration. If a member violates guidelines again after suspension ends, moderators can issue another suspension or escalate to permanent termination.

This operation is exclusively available to moderator accounts. Only users with moderator role can suspend member accounts through this endpoint. Member accounts or guests attempting to access this endpoint receive HTTP 403 Forbidden response.

operations.specification: This operation permanently bans a member account by a moderator, setting the account status to 'terminated' and preventing all future access. It operates on the discussion_board_members table and creates a corresponding moderation action record for audit purposes. The ban is irreversible without administrator intervention and notifies the affected member of the permanent ban decision with the provided reason.
operations.summary: Permanently ban a discussion board member account
operations.description:
Permanently ban a member account from the discussion board system. This operation sets the member's account status to 'terminated', preventing them from logging in or accessing any platform features. The ban is permanent and can only be reversed by system administrators through direct database intervention.

The requesting moderator must provide a detailed ban reason explaining why the member's account is being terminated. This reason is recorded in the audit trail and communicated to the banned member via email notification, ensuring transparency in the moderation decision.

Security and authorization: Only moderators can execute this operation, as it represents the most severe account restriction available. The operation validates that the requesting user has moderator privileges before proceeding. Banning a member account is a significant action and requires careful consideration of the member's behavior history and violation severity.

Business logic and effects: When a member is banned, their account becomes completely inaccessible. The member cannot log in with their credentials, cannot create new articles or comments, and their previously published content remains visible on the platform but is attributed to a deleted/banned user account. The ban timestamp is recorded in the deleted_at field for audit purposes.

Audit trail: A moderation action record is created with action_type 'ban_member', the moderator's identity, the ban reason, and optional notes. This creates an immutable record for dispute resolution, pattern analysis, and accountability of moderator decisions.

Related operations: Before banning a member, moderators typically issue warnings (not exposed via API) or temporary suspensions to allow for behavior correction. The member management dashboard (GET /moderation/dashboard) displays members with moderation history to help identify candidates for banning.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member account to be banned (UUID format)

responseBody.description: Banned member account information with updated status showing termination

This operation retrieves the comprehensive moderation dashboard displaying all pending items requiring moderator action, recent moderation statistics, and system health metrics. It operates as a read-only view aggregating data from discussion_board_articles (pending_approval status), discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_members (for user warnings/suspensions), and discussion_board_moderation_actions tables to provide moderators with actionable insights.

The dashboard prioritizes pending articles awaiting approval, displays content reports, tracks moderation metrics (approval rate, deletion rate, average review time), and provides quick-access statistics about suspended and terminated accounts. All data is calculated in real-time to ensure moderators have the most current system state.
operations.summary: Retrieve the moderation dashboard with pending items and statistics
operations.description:
Access the comprehensive moderation dashboard providing moderators with an overview of all pending moderation tasks and system metrics. This operation aggregates data across multiple tables to present a unified interface for moderator activity management.

The dashboard displays critical information including: pending articles awaiting approval (with count and preview data), recent reports from community members about inappropriate content, current suspension and termination counts, moderation statistics (items approved/rejected/deleted in the current period), and moderator activity metrics.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated moderators can access this dashboard. The operation validates moderator role before returning data. All sensitive information is appropriately filtered (member email addresses shown only in context of moderation decisions, not in summary statistics).

Data aggregation: The dashboard aggregates data from multiple sources including pending article queue (articles with status 'pending_approval'), member activity history, moderation action audit logs, and reported content flags. This aggregation creates a real-time view of system moderation state without requiring multiple separate API calls.

Business context: The dashboard serves as the primary interface for moderators to understand their workload and track community guideline enforcement effectiveness. Metrics displayed help moderators identify patterns (e.g., which members repeatedly violate guidelines, which content categories trigger most deletions) for insights into platform health.

Performance considerations: The dashboard returns aggregated metrics and pagination-ready lists rather than complete datasets. Moderators can drill down into specific pending items using dedicated endpoints. Response includes counts and top items to enable quick decision-making without overwhelming data volume.

Related operations: From the dashboard, moderators navigate to individual article review (GET /articles/{articleId}), member profiles (GET /members/{memberId}), or specific content reports for detailed action. The dashboard serves as the hub for all moderation workflows.

responseBody.description: Moderation dashboard data including pending items, statistics, and actionable metrics for moderators

The operation supports advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination to help moderators manage their review workload efficiently. Articles returned include full details necessary for moderator evaluation: title, body, creator information, category, submission time, and any rejection reason if previously rejected.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion board articles currently pending moderator approval. This operation is the primary interface for moderators to access the content review queue and manage articles awaiting publication decisions.

The operation supports comprehensive search and filtering capabilities including sorting by submission date, article title, category, or creator. Moderators can use pagination to navigate through pending items efficiently. The status filter is automatically applied to return only articles with status='pending_approval', excluding already published, rejected, or archived articles.

Response includes article summary information with creator details, category assignment, submission timestamps, view count, and any previous rejection reason if the article was submitted after initial rejection. This information enables moderators to make informed approval or rejection decisions.

Security and authorization: Only moderators with active status can access this operation. The operation filters articles based on moderation queue state, not user-specific permissions, ensuring all moderators see the complete review queue for transparent workload distribution and consistent moderation across the platform.

It operates on the discussion_board_reports table, providing moderators with a report queue for investigation. The operation supports filtering by report status (pending_review, resolved, dismissed), reason category, and assignment. Moderators use this operation to access reports requiring action, discover patterns of problematic content, and track resolution progress. Reports include details about the reported content type (article or comment), reporter identity, reason for report, description, current status, assigned moderator, and moderation notes.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of member-submitted content reports awaiting moderator investigation and action. This operation provides the primary interface for moderators to access the report queue and manage content flagged by the community as violating guidelines.

The operation supports advanced filtering and sorting including filtering by report status (pending_review, resolved, dismissed), report reason (offensive_language, personal_attack, spam, off_topic, copyright_violation, harassment, other), reported content type (article or comment), reporter identity, and assignment to specific moderators. Moderators can sort by creation date, resolution date, priority, or other relevant criteria.

Response includes comprehensive report details: the report submission timestamp, reported content type and identifier, reporter member information, reason category, detailed description, current status, assigned moderator, moderator notes if any investigation occurred, and resolution timestamp if applicable. This information enables moderators to understand context and take appropriate moderation actions.

Security and authorization: Only moderators with active status can access this operation. The operation returns all reports regardless of assignment status, enabling supervisory overview and workload balancing. Reports form the evidence base for moderation decisions and are immutable audit records.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, searchable, and sortable list of all moderation actions performed on the discussion board. It queries the discussion_board_moderation_actions table to provide moderators and administrators with a comprehensive audit trail of content review decisions, rejections, deletions, and editorial changes. The operation supports filtering by action type, content type, moderator, member, date range, and reason keywords to enable detailed investigation of moderation patterns and decision consistency.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of all discussion board moderation actions
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, filterable list of moderation actions taken on discussion board content. This operation provides moderators and administrators with access to the complete audit trail of all moderation decisions, including article approvals, rejections, deletions, comment removals, and content edits. Each record includes the moderator who performed the action, the affected content, the specific action taken, the business reason, and detailed notes.

The operation supports advanced filtering capabilities including action type (approved, rejected, deleted_article, deleted_comment, etc.), content type (article or comment), moderator assignment, member identification, date ranges, and keyword search in reason and notes fields. Results can be sorted by creation date, action type, or moderator for investigation and pattern analysis.

Pagination is provided with configurable page size to handle large audit trails efficiently. This operation is critical for governance, compliance, and dispute resolution workflows where moderation decisions must be transparent and auditable.

Security: This operation is restricted to moderators who need administrative visibility into moderation history. The moderator accessing this operation can view all moderation actions system-wide without filtering by their own actions, enabling supervisory oversight and consistency review.

Related operations: GET /moderation/actions/{actionId} retrieves a single moderation action detail. PATCH /moderation/member-activity/{memberId} retrieves moderation actions affecting a specific member.

Retrieve the complete moderation history for a specific member, showing all moderation actions taken on their content and account. This operation displays all articles that were approved or rejected, all comments that were deleted, any account status changes (suspensions, warnings, terminations), and any editorial corrections made by moderators to the member's content.

The operation provides context for member disputes or appeals, enabling both moderators and members (with appropriate authorization) to understand why specific content was rejected or removed. It supports filtering by action type and date range to focus on specific moderation events, and results are paginated chronologically from most recent to oldest.

This operation serves multiple use cases: members can view their moderation history and understand why their content was not published; moderators can review moderation patterns against a specific user for consistency analysis and identification of repeat violations; administrators can analyze user behavior and enforcement patterns.

Security: This operation can be accessed by moderators viewing member history for administrative purposes. Members may be able to access their own moderation history through authorization checking in the implementation (checking if requesting member matches memberId in path).

Related operations: PATCH /moderation/actions retrieves system-wide moderation actions with broader filtering. GET /members/{memberId} provides member account information.

Each report captures the reported content reference (either article or comment), the reason for the report, optional detailed description, and the reporting member's identity. The report is then queued for moderator review. This operation implements the member reporting mechanism described in the Content Moderation Requirements, enabling community participation in content governance while maintaining moderator authority over final decisions.
operations.summary: Create a new member report of inappropriate content for moderator review

This operation allows authenticated members to report articles or comments they believe violate community guidelines. Members submit a report containing a reference to the reported content (either an article or comment), a predefined reason category (offensive_language, personal_attack, spam, off_topic, copyright_violation, harassment, or other), and an optional detailed description (maximum 500 characters) explaining their concern.

When a report is submitted, the system stores it with pending_review status, making it visible in the moderator review queue. The report captures the reporting member's identity for audit purposes and allows moderators to investigate and take appropriate action (deleting content, suspending accounts, or dismissing the report if no violation is found).

Reports are distinct from moderation actions themselves—this operation captures user-generated feedback flagging problematic content, while actual moderation decisions (deletions, suspensions, bans) are handled separately by moderators. This separation enables tracking both member concerns and moderator decisions independently for comprehensive audit trails.

Each report is permanently recorded in the system for audit and moderation history purposes. Members can report the same content multiple times (multiple reports from different members), allowing moderators to see which content has attracted multiple complaints. The status field allows moderators to track report workflow: pending_review (awaiting investigation), resolved (moderator took action), or dismissed (moderator reviewed and found no violation).

The operation supports complex query parameters for filtering pending reports, searching resolved reports by outcome, and analyzing report trends. This implements the moderator queue management system specified in the Content Moderation Requirements, providing moderators with comprehensive visibility into all submitted reports and their investigation status.

This operation provides moderators with a searchable, paginated view of all member reports in the system. Moderators can filter reports by status (pending_review, resolved, dismissed), reason category (offensive_language, personal_attack, spam, off_topic, copyright_violation, harassment, other), date range, and assignment status. The operation supports sorting by report date, resolution time, or reason for analysis and prioritization.

The moderator queue management system relies on this operation to display the reports queue showing items awaiting investigation. Moderators use this endpoint to find pending reports that need attention, view reports they have assigned to themselves, review historical reports for pattern analysis, and track resolution metrics (average resolution time, most common report reasons, etc.).

The response includes report details necessary for moderator decision-making: the reported content summary (article title or comment preview), reporter member name, reason category, optional description provided by reporter, current status, any moderator notes already added, and timestamps of submission and resolution. This comprehensive view allows moderators to quickly assess each report's context and determine appropriate action.

Search capabilities include text search in reporter descriptions and moderator notes, allowing moderators to find reports matching specific keywords or patterns. Pagination supports efficient navigation through potentially hundreds of reports, and sorting options help moderators prioritize high-volume report reasons or identify patterns of problematic content or members.

The operation follows security principles by restricting access to the moderator role only. Members cannot view other members' reports or the reports queue. This protects reporter privacy and prevents gaming of the reporting system.

Fetch comprehensive information about a single content report from the discussion board moderation system. This operation returns complete report details including the member who filed the report, which content was reported (article or comment), the reason category, optional detailed description, current status in the review workflow, assigned moderator information, moderator investigation notes, and all relevant timestamps.

The operation is essential for moderators managing the content review queue and investigating specific reports. When a moderator clicks on a report to review its details, this endpoint provides all necessary context about the report including what content was reported, who reported it and why, and what action (if any) has been taken.

Security and Access Control: This operation requires moderator authentication to access report details. Regular members cannot view reports filed by others (only moderators can investigate). The operation respects the moderation workflow by providing different visibility based on user role - only authenticated moderators can invoke this endpoint.

Relationships to Underlying Database: The operation pulls data from the discussion_board_reports table which maintains references to discussion_board_members (the reporter), discussion_board_articles (if report is about an article), discussion_board_comments (if report is about a comment), and discussion_board_moderators (assigned moderator). These relationships enable the response to include context about all entities involved in the report.

Business Logic: Reports progress through defined status states (pending_review, resolved, dismissed) tracked in the status field. The resolved_at timestamp indicates when a moderator completed their investigation. The moderator_notes field captures the moderator's reasoning for their resolution decision, supporting audit trails and consistent moderation decisions.

Submit a new report about a published article that the member believes violates community guidelines or policies. This operation creates a report record that enters the moderator review queue and notifies moderators to investigate the reported content.

The operation captures why the member filed the report (using predefined reason categories: offensive_language, personal_attack, spam, off_topic, copyright_violation, harassment, other), includes optional detailed context explaining the violation, and associates the report with both the reporting member and the reported article.

Security and Access Control: Only authenticated members can file reports, preventing anonymous submissions and enabling moderator follow-up with reporters if needed. Each report captures the filing member's identity for audit purposes. Members can report any published article they encounter, not just articles by specific users, enabling community moderation support.

Relationships and Workflow: The created report enters pending_review status and appears in the moderator queue for investigation. Reports reference both the discussion_board_members table (reporter identity) and discussion_board_articles table (the reported content). The report remains in the system as a permanent audit record even after moderators resolve it, tracking all community feedback about content quality.

Validation and Business Rules: Reports must specify a reason from the predefined category list to ensure consistent triage. The optional description field (maximum 500 characters) provides context for moderators. The operation initializes the report with pending_review status, null moderator_notes (no investigation yet), and null resolved_at timestamp (not yet resolved). Reports are permanent audit records tracking member concerns and community feedback. The combination of discussion_board_member_id (reporter), discussion_board_comment_id (reported content), reason, and timestamps enables moderators to analyze reporting patterns, prioritize high-impact issues, and maintain community standards.

Assign a pending report to a moderator for investigation and resolution. This operation updates the report's assigned_moderator_id field, transitioning the report from unassigned to assigned state. Only moderators with appropriate permissions can assign reports.

When a report is assigned, the moderator takes responsibility for investigating the reported content, reviewing the reporter's reason and description, examining the flagged comment or article, and determining appropriate action (keeping content as-is, editing content, or removing content). The assignment captures moderator accountability for report resolution.

Reports can be reassigned from one moderator to another if needed. The assignment operation does not change the report's status (remains 'pending_review') - status transitions to 'resolved' or 'dismissed' only when the moderator completes their investigation and takes final action.

Security: Only moderators can assign reports. The operation validates that the target moderator exists and is active. Assignment timestamps are recorded for audit purposes. The moderator assignment enables tracking which moderator is responsible for each report's resolution.

The moderator performing this action records their final decision, including notes about the investigation outcome and any actions taken regarding the reported content. This operation operates on the discussion_board_reports table and marks the completion of a moderation review workflow. The report's resolved_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time, and the assigned_moderator_id is set based on the authenticated moderator. Resolve a discussion board report by updating its status to 'resolved' and recording the moderator's investigation findings. This operation completes the moderation review workflow for a report that was pending investigation.

The moderator performing this action must provide resolution notes explaining their decision and any actions taken regarding the reported content. These notes become part of the permanent audit trail and may be shared with affected members to explain moderation decisions.

Upon resolution, the report's status changes from 'pending_review' to 'resolved', the resolved_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time, and the report is removed from the moderator's active queue. This operation is part of the moderation workflow defined in the discussion_board_reports table, where reports progress from pending_review through resolution or dismissal.

The report being resolved must exist and must currently have a status of 'pending_review'. The authenticated moderator must have appropriate permissions to resolve reports. This operation preserves the complete audit trail including the moderator who performed the action, the timestamp, and detailed notes for accountability and dispute resolution.
